notes: Every volume, difficulty, cpc and parentTopic value in this file is a raw Ahrefs keywords-explorer-matching-terms figure for the stated country. Nothing is estimated or interpolated.
Ahrefs cost was 23 units per returned row (volume + difficulty are 10 units each). 33588 units were spent across 20 matching-terms calls plus 1 free subscription check.

Method: keywords-explorer-matching-terms, match_mode=terms, order_by=volume:desc, with a minimum-volume filter per market (gb 50-60, jp/tw/id 20-30, kr 20-30, tr 20-30) and a per-call row cap, so that units were not spent on zero-volume rows.

Deduplication: every row was checked against data/keyword-research.json on (country, lowercased, whitespace-normalised keyword). 1 row(s) collided with the existing set and were dropped; 1 row(s) were duplicates within this pass. en-gb was deduped only against existing gb rows, not against us rows.

All 1224 kept rows have a real integer volume. 728 rows have difficulty = null, 482 have cpc = null and 728 have parentTopic = null, because Ahrefs itself returned null for those fields. Nulls are excluded from every total (volume totals are unaffected since no volume is null).

Relevance filter: kept travel eSIM, travel connectivity, mobile data abroad, roaming, travel SIM, competitor brands (airalo, holafly, nomad, saily, ubigi, maya, jetpac, roamless, roamic, klook, kkday, trifa, DJB, Dosirak, World eSIM) and eSIM device / troubleshooting queries. Dropped: purely domestic carrier eSIM provisioning (Telkomsel / XL / Smartfren / Indosat / by.U migration and registration in id, KT / SKT / LG U+ / MVNO activation in kr, docomo / ahamo / povo / UQ / mineo / IIJmio / Rakuten setup in jp, Turkcell / Turk Telekom provisioning in tr, Chunghwa domestic eSIM setup in tw), and non-telecom homonyms of 漫遊 in tw (the novel Taiwan Travelogue, 2001: A Space Odyssey, a campsite, a comic).

Carrier-brand queries were KEPT when they are about using that carrier abroad (for example ソフトバンク esim 海外, ahamo 海外 esim, kt 해외 로밍, 中華電信日本漫遊, vodafone travel esim, o2 travel esim, lebara travel esim). Those are roaming substitution demand, which is exactly what a travel eSIM displaces.

HONESTY FLAG - Taiwan: 49 of the 289 tw rows are 漫遊 (roaming) queries worth 90700 searches/month, i.e. 57 percent of the tw total. These are Taiwanese users pricing their own carrier's international roaming (Chunghwa Telecom, Taiwan Mobile, FarEasTone). They are real travel-connectivity demand and a real substitution target, but they are NOT people searching for a travel eSIM, and they will be hard to convert.

HONESTY FLAG - generic heads: the bare term "esim" was kept for kr, id and tr and accounts for 71000 searches/month on its own. In Indonesia in particular the bare head is dominated by domestic carrier intent (esim telkomsel alone is 38000/mo in the same country), so treat that 40000 as category awareness, not travel demand.

HONESTY FLAG - Korea: 이심 해외 and esim 구매 returned only 9 and 17 rows above 20/mo. Korean travel eSIM long tail is genuinely thin in Korean script. The volume that does exist sits under the plain Latin term "esim" and under destination terms (일본 esim, 중국 esim, 미국 esim, 대만 esim, 베트남 esim). Head terms used for kr therefore include a broad "esim" sweep.

HONESTY FLAG - Indonesia: esim luar negeri returned 6 rows and roaming luar negeri returned 2 rows. Outbound-travel eSIM demand in Indonesian is close to non-existent today. Real Indonesian eSIM volume is domestic carrier volume, which was filtered out. The travel-relevant id rows are mostly ENGLISH-language inbound queries about Bali (bali esim, best esim for bali, esim bali tourist), which is a different customer: the foreign visitor, not the Indonesian traveller.

HONESTY FLAG - Turkey: yurtdışı esim, esim türkiye and esim satın al returned 13, 14 and 1 rows respectively. A broad "esim" sweep was substituted as the fourth head term. Most measurable tr volume is INBOUND: esim turkey, esim türkei, esim turquie, esim turcja, esim turchia, esim turkije, esim turquia, esim турция are foreign-language queries by tourists coming to Turkey, with CPCs of 130-350 cents. Those rows carry their detected language, not "tr".

Cross-language rows were labelled by detected language rather than by market default: 8 non-Turkish inbound rows in tr (de, fr, pl, it, nl, es, ru), English brand and inbound rows in tr, kr and id, and Japanese-script rows measured in kr (esim 韓国, 韓国 esim, 日本 esim, esim 繋がらない, 日本 esim 一時帰国, esim 日本に着いたら) which are Japanese travellers searching inside Korea.

Head-term selection deviated from "top 4 by existing volume" in three places, and the deviations are listed in headTermsUsed. jp: esim 海外 and esim 韓国 were used instead of iphone esim and esim ヨーロッパ because they are the genuine outbound-travel heads for Japan; esim 韓国 alone returned 14000/mo. tw: 漫遊 was used in place of samsung esim to cover roaming. kr, id and tr each received an extra broad "esim" sweep because their native-language heads were too thin to produce a usable long tail.

Competitor brand coverage found in this pass: airalo, holafly, nomad, saily, ubigi, maya, jetpac, roamless, roamic, pocket esim, esim.io (tr), Klook, KKday, DJB, trifa (jp/tw), World eSIM (jp), Dosirak (kr), Studio A and 酷遊卡 (tw). esim io at 8100/mo in tr is the single largest competitor-brand term found.
Nothing was measured for ae, sa, ru, us or the Tier 1 European markets in this pass; they were explicitly out of scope for this agent.

Not measured and therefore absent: SERP features, traffic potential, global volume, and monthly volume history. Only volume, difficulty, cpc and parent_topic were requested, to keep the unit cost at 23 per row.
